title: A written talk becomes a captioned clip
pitch: Three lines of script in. Two voices, a set, a waveform and captions timed by what was actually said out.
why: Kokoro reads the lines in two voices, Z-Image makes the empty set, and Whisper listens to the finished audio, so the captions come from what was said, not from the script.

fields.label: First voice
fields.default: Welcome back to Small Rooms. Today we are talking about why an old wooden chair creaks.

fields.label: Second voice
fields.default: It is the joints. Wood shrinks a little every winter, the glue lets go, and every time you sit down, two pieces rub.

fields.label: First voice again
fields.default: So the fix is new glue, not more nails. Thanks for listening.

models.name: ffmpeg
models.licence: LGPL/GPL, runs as a separate tool

tips: Write the lines the way you want them said; the captions come from the audio, so a misread word shows.

steps.label: The conversation
steps.does: The three lines one after another, with a short pause.

57:27.text: An empty small podcast studio corner, two microphones on boom arms over a wooden table, warm lamps, wood panelled wall, soft evening light, no people, nothing written anywhere.

steps.label: Picture and waveform
steps.does: The set with a waveform drawn from the real audio.

steps.label: Captions
steps.does: Whisper writes timed captions from what it hears.

steps.label: Captions on
steps.does: Burns the captions into the clip.
